metadata.title: Politician Profiles — 100 Leaders
metadata.structure: Flat list of profile objects; not grouped by country
metadata.note: Entries follow the provided source text as-is, which contains some alternate-scenario claims (e.g., Barack Obama listed as sitting U.S. president, Angela Rayner as U.K. prime minister).

profiles.name: Genghis Khan
profiles.title: Founder & Great Khan of the Mongol Empire
profiles.summary: Founder of the largest contiguous land empire in history. He unified the nomadic tribes of Northeast Asia and reshaped global trade, demographics, and cross-continental communication through immense military strategy.

profiles.name: Alexander the Great
profiles.title: King of Macedon
profiles.summary: Undefeated military tactician. He conquered the Persian Empire and expanded Hellenistic civilization across Greece, Egypt, and into western India, permanently blending Western and Eastern cultures.

profiles.name: Julius Caesar
profiles.title: General & Dictator of the Roman Republic
profiles.summary: Architect of the Roman Empire. His aggressive military expansions through Gaul and masterful political maneuvering effectively dismantled the Roman Republic, laying the institutional foundation for the Pax Romana.

profiles.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
profiles.title: Emperor of the French
profiles.summary: Global legal and military reformer. Beyond conquering most of continental Europe, he codified the Napoleonic Code, which established modern civic legal frameworks used across dozens of countries today.

profiles.name: Abraham Lincoln
profiles.title: 16th President of the United States
profiles.summary: The premier democratic unifier. He preserved the Union during the American Civil War, abolished slavery via the Emancipation Proclamation, and redefined the modern constitutional governance framework.

profiles.name: Vladimir Putin
profiles.title: President of the Russian Federation
profiles.summary: Russia's dominant leader, wielding centralized authority over the state, security services, and foreign policy across Eurasia and beyond.

profiles.name: Mikhail Mishustin
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Russia
profiles.summary: Head of government overseeing Russia's civil administration, economic management, and federal policy execution.

profiles.name: Sergey Lavrov
profiles.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Russia
profiles.summary: Russia's veteran diplomat and chief voice on the world stage, directing foreign policy across decades of global realignment.

profiles.name: Andrey Belousov
profiles.title: Minister of Defence of Russia
profiles.summary: Head of the defense establishment and former First Deputy Prime Minister, steering Russia's wartime economy and military strategy.

profiles.name: Sergey Sobyanin
profiles.title: Mayor of Moscow
profiles.summary: Chief executive of the Russian capital, overseeing megacity administration, urban development, and security coordination.

profiles.name: Dmitry Peskov
profiles.title: Presidential Press Secretary / Kremlin Spokesperson
profiles.summary: The Kremlin's principal voice, shaping official narratives and communicating the leadership's positions to the world.

profiles.name: Dmitry Medvedev
profiles.title: Deputy Chairman of the Security Council
profiles.summary: Former President and Prime Minister now holding a senior security-state role, known for hardline national-security rhetoric.

profiles.name: Vyacheslav Volodin
profiles.title: Chairman of the State Duma
profiles.summary: Speaker of Russia's lower house of parliament, controlling the legislative agenda and floor proceedings.

profiles.name: Gennady Zyuganov
profiles.title: Leader of the Communist Party of the Russian Federation
profiles.party: Communist Party of the Russian Federation (CPRF)
profiles.summary: Longtime leader of Russia's principal opposition communist party and a fixture of national parliamentary politics.

profiles.name: Valentina Matviyenko
profiles.title: Chairperson of the Federation Council
profiles.summary: Speaker of Russia's upper house and one of the highest-ranking officials in the country's political establishment.

profiles.name: Narendra Modi
profiles.title: Prime Minister of India
profiles.summary: Head of government and BJP leader, commanding large-scale national policymaking and India's strategic direction on the world stage.

profiles.name: Yogi Adityanath
profiles.title: Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh
profiles.summary: Head of India's most populous state and a prominent national figure within the BJP's political movement.

profiles.name: J.P. Nadda
profiles.title: National President of the BJP
profiles.summary: Party chief directing the organizational machinery and electoral strategy of India's ruling party.

profiles.name: Mallikarjun Kharge
profiles.title: President of the Indian National Congress; Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha
profiles.summary: Leads India's main opposition party and its parliamentary bloc in the upper house, anchoring the anti-incumbent alliance.

profiles.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Israel
profiles.summary: Israel's longest-serving leader, heading the incumbent right-wing government through a volatile security and political era.

profiles.name: Gadi Eisenkot
profiles.title: Party Leader, Yashar
profiles.summary: Former IDF Chief of Staff leading a major center-right/centrist challenge to Netanyahu.

profiles.name: Naftali Bennett
profiles.title: Party Co-Leader, Beyachad (Together)
profiles.summary: Former Prime Minister who returned to frontline politics via an alliance with Yair Lapid.

profiles.name: Yair Lapid
profiles.title: Opposition Leader; Leader, Yesh Atid
profiles.summary: Former Prime Minister and leader of the central opposition bloc.

profiles.name: Benny Gantz
profiles.title: Party Leader, Blue and White
profiles.summary: Former Defense Minister and former IDF Chief of Staff leading a centrist security-focused party.

profiles.name: Itamar Ben-Gvir
profiles.title: National Security Minister; Leader, Otzma Yehudit
profiles.summary: Far-right National Security Minister advocating a hardline security platform.

profiles.name: Bezalel Smotrich
profiles.title: Finance Minister; Leader, Religious Zionist Party
profiles.summary: Finance Minister and prominent figure of the national-religious right.

profiles.name: Aryeh Deri
profiles.title: Leader, Shas
profiles.summary: Leader of the ultra-Orthodox Sephardic Shas party and key coalition powerbroker.

profiles.name: Avigdor Lieberman
profiles.title: Party Leader, Yisrael Beiteinu
profiles.summary: Secular right-wing opposition leader and former defense and foreign minister.

profiles.name: Yair Golan
profiles.title: Party Leader, The Democrats
profiles.summary: Former senior IDF commander leading the merged left-of-center Democratic party bloc.

profiles.name: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi
profiles.title: President of Egypt
profiles.summary: Commands the most powerful military force in Africa, exerting immense regional authority over Red Sea and North African geopolitics with an uncompromising approach to state security.

profiles.name: Paul Kagame
profiles.title: President of Rwanda
profiles.summary: Regarded as one of Africa's most formidable leaders, globally recognized for highly disciplined governance and sharp rebukes of Western interference.

profiles.name: Abiy Ahmed
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
profiles.summary: Controls the Horn of Africa's dominant military power, known for assertive foreign policy and open defiance of neighboring coalitions over Red Sea access and regional sovereignty.

profiles.name: Ibrahim Traoré
profiles.title: Head of the Military Junta of Burkina Faso
profiles.summary: Populist military leader who seized power in a coup, aggressively deploying anti-colonial pan-African rhetoric backed by heavily fortified presidential security.

profiles.name: Assimi Goïta
profiles.title: Head of the Military Junta of Mali
profiles.summary: Core figure of West Africa's shift toward military governance, having severed traditional European defense ties in favor of alternative security partnerships.

profiles.name: Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo
profiles.title: President of Equatorial Guinea
profiles.summary: The world's longest-serving current president, maintaining absolute internal authority and strict security structures to insulate his regime from dissent.

profiles.name: Yoweri Museveni
profiles.title: President of Uganda
profiles.summary: In power since 1986, commanding a formidable regional military intelligence network and using state power to suppress domestic opposition.

profiles.name: Isaias Afwerki
profiles.title: President of Eritrea
profiles.summary: Heads a highly militarized, closed state structure, maintaining total domestic authority through compulsory national service and isolationist policies.

profiles.name: Julius Malema
profiles.title: Leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters
profiles.summary: Not a head of state, but widely considered one of Africa's most powerful and rhetorically aggressive politicians, commanding influence via radical economic and populist anti-establishment platforms.

profiles.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
profiles.title: President of Zimbabwe
profiles.summary: Known as "The Crocodile," he maintains an unyielding grip on political power backed by state security forces to deter opposition movements.

profiles.name: Xi Jinping
profiles.title: General Secretary of the CCP; President of China; Chairman of the Central Military Commission
profiles.summary: China's Paramount Leader, wielding absolute authority over the party, state, and military. Considered the nation's most powerful ruler since Mao Zedong.

profiles.name: Li Qiang
profiles.title: Premier of the State Council
profiles.summary: Head of China's government holding the highest civil service rank, overseeing the state bureaucracy, economic policy coordination, and execution of national development plans.

profiles.name: Zhao Leji
profiles.title: Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee
profiles.summary: Head of China's legislature, leading the top state body responsible for legislation, constitutional supervision, and high-level foreign diplomatic outreach.

profiles.name: Mark Carney
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Canada
profiles.summary: Head of government after taking office following Justin Trudeau's resignation and winning a national mandate. The former Governor of the Bank of Canada and Bank of England commands authority over the federal bureaucracy, focusing on economic strategy and trade and tariff dynamics.

profiles.name: Pierre Poilievre
profiles.title: Leader of the Conservative Party / Leader of the Opposition
profiles.summary: Leader of the Official Opposition, commanding a powerful conservative movement centered on a low-tax, small-government platform as the primary challenger to the government.

profiles.name: Lee Jae-myung
profiles.title: President of South Korea
profiles.summary: Head of state and government after winning the early snap election, with control of the executive branch and parliament. His administration centers on national reconciliation, welfare expansion, economic stabilization, and de-escalating tensions with North Korea.

profiles.name: Kim Min-seok
profiles.title: Prime Minister of South Korea
profiles.summary: Second-in-command of the executive branch, overseeing the domestic civil service and state administrative coordination, and executing the ruling party's legislative and economic priorities.

profiles.name: Woo Won-shik
profiles.title: Speaker of the National Assembly
profiles.summary: Head of the legislative branch, controlling the National Assembly's agenda and holding immense influence over budgets, policy initiatives, and regulatory updates.

profiles.name: Kim Jong Un
profiles.title: General Secretary of the WPK; President of the State Affairs Commission; Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces
profiles.summary: Supreme Leader of North Korea and third generational ruler of the Kim dynasty, maintaining total absolute control over party, state, and military. Every major directive, foreign policy shift, and strategic nuclear decision flows from his command.

profiles.name: Kim Tok Hun
profiles.title: Premier of the Cabinet
profiles.summary: Head of government and Presidium Politburo member, overseeing civil administration, the national economy, and state production, frequently conducting high-level inspections for the central leadership.

profiles.name: Donald Trump
profiles.title: President of the United States
profiles.summary: Ranked Europe's most powerful figure by POLITICO despite being outside the continent, due to supreme leverage over European defense budgets, NATO strategic shifts, and trade tariffs.

profiles.name: Mette Frederiksen
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Denmark
profiles.summary: "The North Star." A dominant, pragmatic voice leading smaller European nations in hardline border management, defense scaling, and standing firm against security pressures.

profiles.name: Friedrich Merz
profiles.title: Chancellor of Germany
profiles.summary: "The Reluctant Radical." Wields immense clout as leader of Europe's largest economy, executing immigration rollbacks and industrial adjustments to keep Germany competitive.

profiles.name: Marine Le Pen
profiles.title: Leader of National Rally
profiles.summary: "The Warhorse." Holds immense disruptive power over French and European legislative spaces, driving the continent-wide surge toward populist right-wing governance and standing as a frontrunner for the 2027 presidential race.

profiles.name: Nigel Farage
profiles.title: Leader of Reform UK
profiles.summary: "The Populist Trailblazer." A highly influential right-wing provocateur whose populist rhetoric continues to disrupt mainstream politics across the UK and continental Europe.

profiles.name: Ursula von der Leyen
profiles.title: President of the European Commission
profiles.summary: "The Institutional Architect." Oversees the EU's executive arm, directing massive continental climate investments, security frameworks, and regulatory mandates.

profiles.name: Mark Rutte
profiles.title: Secretary-General of NATO
profiles.summary: "The Transatlantic Anchor." The former Dutch PM guides Europe's military alliance, balancing European sovereignty with volatile defense dependencies.

profiles.name: Giorgia Meloni
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Italy
profiles.summary: "The Right-Wing Pragmatist." Blends staunch nationalist policies with functional pro-Brussels diplomacy, proving highly influential on continental migration pacts.

profiles.name: Keir Starmer
profiles.title: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (per the Europe ranking)
profiles.summary: "The Centrist Counterweight." Directs the UK's massive geopolitical repositioning as a stable, rule-based ally seeking closer security pacts with European nations.

profiles.name: Anthony Albanese
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Australia
profiles.summary: Head of government and Labor leader, commanding the party and directing national policy, legislative agendas, and the government's broader direction.

profiles.name: Jim Chalmers
profiles.title: Federal Treasurer of Australia
profiles.summary: Wields immense institutional power over the national economy, managing the federal budget, economic strategy, and major tax policy updates.

profiles.name: Peter Dutton
profiles.title: Leader of the Opposition; Head of the Liberal Party
profiles.summary: The primary political challenger to the government, coordinating the opposition bloc's parliamentary strategy and wielding significant sway over conservative policy.

profiles.name: Penny Wong
profiles.title: Minister for Foreign Affairs; Leader of the Government in the Senate
profiles.summary: Shapes Australia's international diplomacy, driving critical strategic relations across the Pacific and managing the government's foreign policy framework.

profiles.name: Mark Butler
profiles.title: Minister for Health and Aged Care
profiles.summary: A dominant legislative force managing key high-stakes federal spending portfolios, including major overhauls to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS).

profiles.name: Emmanuel Macron
profiles.title: President of France
profiles.summary: Head of state and commander-in-chief, managing France's executive strategy, foreign policy, and global representation while navigating a deeply polarized national landscape.

profiles.name: Sébastien Lecornu
profiles.title: Prime Minister of France
profiles.summary: Head of government appointed after serving as Defense Minister, tasked with building consensus across a highly fractured parliament to pass national budgets.

profiles.name: Angela Rayner
profiles.title: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (per the U.K. ranking)
profiles.summary: Head of state and government after stepping into 10 Downing Street, balancing centrist and left-wing party factions while directing the state apparatus and international trade and security negotiations.

profiles.name: Rachel Reeves
profiles.title: Chancellor of the Exchequer
profiles.summary: Chief fiscal officer of the UK, holding decisive power over the national budget and economic strategy.

profiles.name: Kemi Badenoch
profiles.title: Leader of the Opposition / Conservative Party
profiles.summary: Leader of the UK opposition, directing the Conservative Party's strategy as its principal counterweight to the government.

profiles.name: Shehbaz Sharif
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Pakistan
profiles.summary: Head of government holding direct institutional power over civil administration, economic stabilization programs, and federal policy execution.

profiles.name: Imran Khan
profiles.title: Founder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf; Opposition Leader
profiles.summary: PTI founder who, despite legal challenges and incarceration, retains massive highly passionate public popularity as the primary anti-establishment populist symbol.

profiles.name: Asif Ali Zardari
profiles.title: President of Pakistan
profiles.summary: Head of state and PPP co-chairman, acting as a master political strategist and the crucial powerbroker anchoring the governing coalition.

profiles.name: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari
profiles.title: Chairman of the Pakistan Peoples Party
profiles.summary: Next-generation leader driving the legislative and structural direction of one of Pakistan's largest mainstream parties, holding a firm stronghold in Sindh province.

profiles.name: Barack Obama
profiles.title: President of the United States (per the provided text)
profiles.summary: Head of state and government per the source text, ranking first in its U.S. power list — commanding authority over the executive branch, the military, and the direction of the Democratic Party.

profiles.name: JD Vance
profiles.title: Vice President of the United States
profiles.summary: Second-in-command of the executive branch and constitutional President of the Senate, a primary architect of the administration's populist economic and domestic policy framework.

profiles.name: Mike Johnson
profiles.title: Speaker of the House
profiles.summary: Head of the legislative branch, controlling the House calendar, budget negotiations, and bill scheduling, with immense leverage over federal spending.

profiles.name: John Thune
profiles.title: Senate Majority Leader
profiles.summary: Senate gatekeeper directing the legislative agenda, controlling floor votes, and overseeing confirmations of executive appointments and judicial nominations.

profiles.name: Hakeem Jeffries
profiles.title: House Minority Leader
profiles.summary: Highest-ranking Black lawmaker in U.S. history, wielding institutional control over House Democratic strategy, legislative resistance, and unified voting blocs.

profiles.name: Wes Moore
profiles.title: Governor of Maryland
profiles.summary: As Maryland's first Black governor, he manages a major state bureaucracy with executive authority over large fiscal budgets, law enforcement, and public policy.

profiles.name: Tim Scott
profiles.title: U.S. Senator (South Carolina)
profiles.summary: Leading Black conservative powerbroker with major sway over financial regulatory frameworks in the Senate and national influence as an architect of conservative economic policy.

profiles.name: Jerome Powell
profiles.title: Chair of the Federal Reserve
profiles.summary: Economic architect wielding immense control over the global economy through monetary policy, interest rates, and financial regulation.

profiles.name: Elon Musk
profiles.title: Government Efficiency Advisor
profiles.summary: External system disruptor wielding substantial influence over federal bureaucracy streamlining, regulatory structures, and industrial tech policy.

profiles.name: Ron DeSantis
profiles.title: Governor of Florida
profiles.summary: State executive leader shaping the conservative movement's national culture war and state-level legislative strategies.

profiles.name: Gavin Newsom
profiles.title: Governor of California
profiles.summary: Progressive counterweight leading the nation's most populous state, using California's economic weight to implement progressive templates on climate and civil rights.

profiles.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
profiles.title: U.S. Representative
profiles.summary: Grassroots ideologue and highly influential progressive communicator, shifting mainstream debates on climate action and economic reform from within Congress.

profiles.name: Sajith Premadasa
profiles.title: Leader of the Opposition; Leader of the SJB
profiles.summary: Heads the Samagi Jana Balawegaya, the primary centrist legislative counterweight to the Marxist-leaning NPP government.

profiles.name: Vijitha Herath
profiles.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs
profiles.summary: Key ruling strategist directing international diplomacy and managing regional ties between India and China for the NPP government.

profiles.name: Namal Rajapaksa
profiles.title: Opposition Member of Parliament
profiles.summary: Next-generation leader of a major political family wielding significant backbench influence while rebuilding the traditionalist SLPP movement.

profiles.name: Tshering Tobgay
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Bhutan
profiles.summary: Head of government overseeing the executive cabinet, state development, and crucial bilateral economic pacts with India under Bhutan's democratic monarchy.

profiles.name: Sangay Dorji
profiles.title: Chairperson of the National Council
profiles.summary: Commands Bhutan's non-partisan upper house of parliament, ensuring legislative checks and balancing regional interests.

profiles.name: Balendra Shah
profiles.title: Prime Minister of Nepal (per the provided text)
profiles.summary: The Populist Youth Wave. The former structural engineer and hip-hop star became Nepal's youngest-ever prime minister after a massive youth-led electoral upsurge, named to the TIME 100 list — a radical pushback against traditional South Asian dynastic politics.

profiles.name: Dr. Mohamed Muizzu
profiles.title: President of the Maldives
profiles.summary: Holds consolidated executive control over the Indian Ocean archipelago, pivoting its strategic infrastructure alignment and defense policies.

profiles.name: Min Aung Hlaing
profiles.title: President & Junta Leader of Myanmar
profiles.summary: Formalized absolute civilian and military authority over Myanmar through a military junta structure, challenged by a shadow civil government and ethnic coalitions.

profiles.name: Aung San Suu Kyi
profiles.title: Detained Democracy Icon (National League for Democracy)
profiles.summary: Under arrest by the military junta, she retains massive public legitimacy and symbolic power over Myanmar's pro-democracy movement.

profiles.name: Zainul Abedin Farroque
profiles.title: Senior Adviser to the BNP; former Opposition Chief Whip
profiles.summary: Veteran six-term MP from Noakhali and former Opposition Chief Whip, famous for his vocal street-level opposition role after being brutally assaulted by police during the 2011 hartal — an event that became a symbolic flashpoint of state-led crackdowns on opposition politicians.

profiles.name: Zillur Rahman
profiles.title: 19th President of Bangladesh
profiles.summary: Highly revered institutional statesman and senior Awami League Presidium member and General Secretary, remembered as a unifying consensus-builder who kept his party unified through the high-stakes 2007–2008 political transitions.

profiles.name: Shamim Osman
profiles.title: Former Member of Parliament (Narayanganj-4)
profiles.summary: Controversial regional strongman credited with coining the famous slogan "Khela Hobe" ("The game is on"). Following the August 5, 2024 political transition, he fled into hiding and faces charges including a trial at International Crimes Tribunal-1 for allegedly leading armed crackdowns during the mass uprisings.

profiles.name: Fazlur Rahman
profiles.title: Politician
profiles.summary: Professionally nicknamed "Fozu Pagla" for his explosive speaking style, he sparked massive political turmoil after claiming the right-wing Jamaat-e-Islami single-handedly orchestrated the July Revolution, triggering temporary suspension directives within his own party and pushback from student coalitions.

profiles.name: Sophie Scholl
profiles.title: Co-founder of The White Rose Society
profiles.summary: Icon of anti-Nazi resistance. As a University of Munich student she co-founded a non-violent student resistance group and distributed underground leaflets exposing Nazi atrocities, becoming a global symbol of moral courage after being executed by the regime.

profiles.name: Wang Dan
profiles.title: Student Leader, Tiananmen Square Protests
profiles.summary: Face of the global pro-democracy movement. As a Peking University history student he organized independent student unions and coordinated the Tiananmen Square protests, topping the government's most-wanted list while leading millions in demands for free speech and political reform.

profiles.name: John Lewis
profiles.title: Co-founder of SNCC; Civil Rights Congressman
profiles.summary: Architect of desegregation. He co-founded the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, organized the Greensboro sit-ins and Freedom Rides, and endured brutal beatings to force the landmark Voting Rights Act.
